### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**1** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **137** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c90f9fb6e21809430db13371d8929a21e6787a8d` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `788a0341e358e4e3874d63020facf55e0a6ec92c` — the merge of head `64e5e460ea64aebec3ddc2442d2ee9996b1a445c` into base `c90f9fb6e21809430db13371d8929a21e6787a8d`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 788a0341e358e4e3874d63020facf55e0a6ec92c && git checkout 788a0341e358e4e3874d63020facf55e0a6ec92c
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin c90f9fb6e21809430db13371d8929a21e6787a8d 64e5e460ea64aebec3ddc2442d2ee9996b1a445c && git checkout -B drift-repro c90f9fb6e21809430db13371d8929a21e6787a8d && git merge --no-ff 64e5e460ea64aebec3ddc2442d2ee9996b1a445c

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c90f9fb6e21809430db13371d8929a21e6787a8d
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `64e5e460ea64aebec3ddc2442d2ee9996b1a445c`
Local-runs: none

Inputs: card #20841 (body and both comments: the dispatch claim and the os-dev-report), PR #20851 (body, file list, net diff `origin/main...` at the head, `origin/main` = `c90f9fb6e`), and the check-runs on the head. Every factual claim below was checked against `origin/main` with `git show` / `git grep`, never the shared working tree.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Accept set: unchanged — RIGHT.** The one `.ts` hunk (`packages/spec/src/ai/solution-blueprint.zod.ts:189`) replaces only the string argument of `.describe()`; the key stays `z.string().optional()` on `BlueprintNavItemSchema`. No key, closed-set member, regex, export or registration is added or removed anywhere in the diff, so the four widening tells are all absent and the card's "⛔ No schema change" holds. A label-less blueprint nav item parses exactly as before.
- **Public surface: unchanged — RIGHT.** No export added, removed or renamed; `Type Check · consumer gates` (the job hosting `check:api-surface`) reads success on the head.
- **What the diff does publish — named correctly.** The field's runtime `.description` string (shipped in the `@objectstack/spec` bundle and in the JSON schema the package builds from it) and the reference page `content/docs/references/ai/solution-blueprint.mdx`. Both are description-only; a patch-level change (see ②).
- **The new describe's factual claims, each checked against `origin/main`:**
  - "absent ⇒ the entry inherits the CURRENT label of what it opens at render time; present ⇒ rendered verbatim": matches the runtime field's own describe on the module-local `BaseNavItemSchema.label` (`packages/spec/src/ui/app.zod.ts:320-326`: "absent ⇒ the entry inherits the CURRENT label of what it opens at render time … a present label renders verbatim and is never overwritten … nothing is materialised for the absent case") and its TSDoc. RIGHT.
  - "a renamed target shows its new name": the TSDoc at `app.zod.ts:313-314` states exactly this as the reason nothing is stored for the absent case. RIGHT.
  - "never copy the target's label in as a default": the card's "⛔ An expander does not materialize it", and the PRESENT-is-verbatim half of `packages/spec/src/ui/app-nav-label-optional-inherited.pin.test.ts` (the parse adds nothing; a fill-in-at-parse implementation is named there as the ruling-destroying shape). RIGHT.
  - The text is in the runtime field's own terms and shape ("Optional: absent ⇒ …; present ⇒ …"), which is what the card's "one describe sentence, matching the runtime field's own" asks for.
- **"Restated, not referenced" — RIGHT.** `BaseNavItemSchema` is a non-exported `const` in `app.zod.ts` (no `export` of it or of any constant carrying the text; the string is an inline literal). The card's conditional ("if it can be referenced") therefore resolves to no without widening `app.zod.ts`, which the card ("⛔ No schema change") and the dispatch's file surface (`:189` only) both forbid. `app.zod.ts` is untouched.
- **Generated artefacts — RIGHT and current.** `packages/spec/json-schema/` is gitignored (`.gitignore:63`; no tracked file under it), so the reference page is the only tracked consumer of the describe. That page carries the row twice (`main` lines 56 and 190); both rows changed and each cell equals the describe string as the `.ts` source evaluates it (the `\'` escape renders as an apostrophe). A grep for the old phrase "defaults to the target label" on the review ref hits only the changeset's own quotation of it; no stale copy remains. `Type Check · source gates` (hosting `check:authorable-surface` then `check:docs`) reads success on the head; `Spec property liveness` reads success.
- **Scope and premise — RIGHT.** Three files, exactly the dispatch's file surface (`:189`, what it regenerates, one `.changeset/20841-*.md`). +21/−3, `size/s`. Head repo is the base repo (not a fork). No governed path; `Governed Surface Queue Guard` reads success. `origin/main` moved three commits past the merge-base `1741c5dcb`; none of them touch the three paths or `app.zod.ts`, and a read-only `merge-tree` of the head onto current `main` is conflict-free.
- **Check-runs on the head, as read 2026-09-30T12:06Z** (32 runs). Required contexts: `Build Core` success; `Governed Surface Queue Guard` success; `Lint & Repo Gates`, `Test Core` (6 shards), `Dogfood Regression Gate` (3 shards) and `Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL)` in progress; the `TypeScript Type Check` aggregate had no check-run yet, its legs reading `source gates` success, `consumer gates` success, `debt ledger` and `workspace` in progress. Advisory: `Check Changeset`, `Check PR Size`, `Build Docs`, `Check Documentation Links`, `Dogfood Verify CLI`, `Auto Label`, `Flag docs affected by code changes`, `Spec property liveness`, and the three card/branch claim guards all success; `Console Pin Gate` and `Packed-tarball smoke (opt-in)` skipped. Nothing red. Landing still waits for the in-progress required contexts to conclude success; this record does not arm anything.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/spec: patch` — RIGHT, floor and ceiling. A describe-only fix in a released package: nothing widens the accept set and nothing enters or leaves the public surface, so `minor` is not owed; the description string and the reference page do publish, so `skip-changeset` would be wrong. `Clause-②: no` on the PR body, in the changeset and on the dispatch claim agree; `no` with no arm is the well-formed spelling, and no ADR-0087 disposition marker is owed because nothing is breaking. `Check Changeset` reads success. The changeset body states what changed and why in the terms an upgrading author greps (the old wording, the new meaning, "the key stays `z.string().optional()`").

### ③ Boundary flags

The os-dev-report (card comment `5910843172`) declares `open_questions: []`, four `deviations`, one `out_of_scope_findings` entry and one NOT-MEASURED item in its summary. Each:

1. **"Zone 1 reference-rather-than-restate not taken" — ANSWERED, correct.** Verified above: the runtime describe is an inline literal on a non-exported const; referencing it needs a new export from `app.zod.ts`, which the card and the file surface forbid.
2. **`check:dual-build-cjs-loads` not measured locally — ANSWERED by the head.** `lint.yml:6020` says ci.yml's `Build Core` hosts that gate; `Build Core` reads success on `64e5e460e`. A string inside `.describe()` cannot change whether a `require` entry point loads. Closed.
3. **Built the lint / client-react / objectql closures under the verify lock — ANSWERED.** Extra local build work only; the net diff against `main` is the three intended files with no stray hunk, so nothing from it entered the PR.
4. **Shell slip (an unquoted heredoc ran backticked text, including a bare `pnpm build`, which failed at `turbo: not found` and wrote nothing) — ANSWERED.** Self-reported; the net diff carries no residue and the PR body was re-written and read back identical per the report. No action.
5. **NOT MEASURED: whether the cloud repo's `apply_blueprint` applier materializes the label today — ESCALATED to the PM, not blocking.** Outside this repo and outside the card's direction, which fixes the contract text on the producer side; not answerable from this review's inputs. If the cloud applier does copy the target's label in today, that is a cloud-side defect to file there, against the contract this PR now states.
6. **Out-of-scope finding: `StrictNavItem.label` reads "Nav entry label, or null" (`solution-blueprint.zod.ts:372`) — ESCALATED to the PM with a recommendation.** The dev's "noted, not filed" is defensible on the card's own definition of the trap (the affirmative word "defaults", which the mirror never carried) and the dispatch's file surface excluded that line. But the strict mirror is the `generateObject` output contract the design model writes against — the file's own comment at `:373-380` says this side "is the one that decides" what a proposal can contain — and it does not say that `null` means inherit-at-render, so an AI author reading only the mirror still has no reason to leave the label null. Recommendation: a follow-up card for one describe edit on `:372` ("null ⇒ inherits the target's current label at render time; do not copy the target's label in"), same file, no schema change, so the inheritance loss the card exists for does not re-enter through the generation contract. Not a defect of this PR.
